source.title: 4 Fantasy Football Busts to Avoid: Wide Receivers
source.author: Evan Tarracciano
source.summary: Four receivers whose current draft prices do not sufficiently account for health, role, or offensive uncertainty.

takeaways.label: bust
takeaways.summary: Rice's WR13 cost does not adequately discount knee recovery, availability, off-field, and changing offensive-balance risks.
takeaways.rationale: Rice's WR13 cost does not adequately discount knee recovery, availability, off-field, and changing offensive-balance risks.
risks: He remains Kansas City's most physically imposing receiver when active.

takeaways.label: bust
takeaways.summary: Adams' WR8 finish leaned heavily on 14 touchdowns, making age, lower-body injuries, and likely red-zone regression dangerous at his price.
takeaways.rationale: Adams' WR8 finish leaned heavily on 14 touchdowns, making age, lower-body injuries, and likely red-zone regression dangerous at his price.
risks: His route skill and established Rams role preserve upside.

takeaways.label: bust
takeaways.summary: Watson's talent and expanded opportunity are outweighed by a long injury history and uncertainty that he can sustain lead-receiver volume.
takeaways.rationale: Watson's talent and expanded opportunity are outweighed by a long injury history and uncertainty that he can sustain lead-receiver volume.
risks: Green Bay extended him and lost two competing receivers.

takeaways.label: bust
takeaways.summary: Tate's rookie price assumes a quick breakout in an offense with quarterback, line, and target-competition concerns.
takeaways.rationale: Tate's rookie price assumes a quick breakout in an offense with quarterback, line, and target-competition concerns.
risks: He can become Tennessee's focal point later in the season.
